name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.11.0: cross-checks PostgreSQL 17 closures, SQL and SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against gold SQL. Two opt-in checks, both off by default: verify.shacl_pairs compares an sql_violation of exactly t.<a> <op> t.<b> with a generated SHACL sh:lessThan or sh:lessThanOrEquals property shape in pySHACL (shacl:pair:<id>), limited to NaN-free base numeric columns and unique keys, otherwise not_run; verify.existence_witness reads in PostgreSQL whether keys an alone Cube answer left out in a sampled or chunked V3 pair test have qualifying source rows under the same filters (v3w:pair_witness), one direction only and without changing the pair test, D95 or V4. The shacl-corpus --w3c-suite profile now includes sh:lessThan and sh:lessThanOrEquals; this is the one default-output change. With both options off every other existing output is unchanged. Rerun build, reason, cube, verify and report after upgrading. No business correctness, data completeness, shared MVCC snapshot, runtime attestation or operational V1-V5 promotion is claimed.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
